source_row.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"The time required for the amount or concentration of a drug in the body to decrease by approximately one half.","B":"The time required for a medication to become completely undetectable in every body compartment after one dose.","C":"The scheduled interval between doses, which may be influenced by half-life but is not the definition of half-life.","D":"The time required for an oral medication to reach peak concentration, which is a different pharmacokinetic measure."}}
source_row.rationale: Elimination half-life describes the time for the drug amount or plasma concentration to fall by about 50%; it is not synonymous with a dosing interval or complete elimination time.
source_row.source_detail: Definition section: elimination half-life is the time required for drug concentration in plasma or total amount in the body to decrease by 50 percent. NCBI Bookshelf StatPearls chapter, live clinical reference rechecked 2026-08-15. Reviewed 2026-08-15.

source_row.stem: A nursing student asks what a medication's elimination half-life means. Which explanation is correct?
